statement_frozen_copy.corpus_verbatim: Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that any $f(n)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line, contain $n$ points which form the vertices of a convex $n$-gon. Prove that $f(n)=2^{n-2}+1$. [#107, prize $500]
statement_frozen_copy.note: Must match challenge.json statement_frozen byte-for-byte (statement integrity gate AC-S).

claims.label: UNCONDITIONAL-MATHEMATICAL (PROOF.md section 1, complete: both directions) + MACHINE-CORROBORATED-FINITE-UNIVERSE (comparator part A)
claims.content: (i) There exist 2 points in GP with no convex 3-gon (a 2-point set has no 3 points at all). (ii) Every 3 points in GP form the vertex set of a non-degenerate triangle: GP forces orient != 0. Hence f(3) = 3.

claims.label: UNCONDITIONAL-MATHEMATICAL (PROOF.md section 2, complete case analysis: hull >= 4 case + hull = 3 interior-pair case with the (alpha) line-intersection and (beta) extremality arguments) + MACHINE-CORROBORATED (comparator parts B and C)
claims.content: (i) LOWER: the 4-point GP witness W4 = {(0,0),(6,0),(3,9),(3,2)} has (3,2) strictly inside the triangle of the other three, hence no convex 4-gon (f(4) >= 5). (ii) UPPER: every 5-point GP set contains 4 points in convex position — if the hull has >= 4 vertices, any 4 hull vertices work; if the hull is a triangle ABC with interior points p,q, the line through p,q separates {A,B} from C, and {A,B,p,q} is in convex position (p not in triangle(A,B,q) and q not in triangle(A,B,p) by the line-intersection argument (alpha); A,B not in the triangles of the others by hull extremality (beta)). Hence f(4) = 5.

claims.label: MACHINE-WITNESSED (comparator part B: W4 regenerated and verified from scratch, two-method checker)
claims.content: W4 = {(0,0),(6,0),(3,9),(3,2)}: GP verified (all 4 triples non-collinear, exact integer cross products); the unique 4-subset is NOT in convex position ((3,2) in the closed triangle of the other three).

claims.label: UNCONDITIONAL-MATHEMATICAL (the PROOF.md case analysis) + MACHINE-CORROBORATED (comparator part C: 10^4 uniform random GP 5-sets + adversarial structured sets + EXHAUSTIVE all GP 5-subsets of the 4x4 and 5x5 grids — zero failures)
claims.content: Every 5-point GP set contains a convex 4-subset. The comparator's sweeps are corroboration over its finite universe (integer grids + random boxes); the mathematical theorem over R^2 is the complete PROOF.md proof.

claims.label: MACHINE-WITNESSED (comparator part D: five 8-point GP witnesses, every one with all C(8,5)=56 subsets swept by the two-method checker, zero convex 5-gons; re-derivation sweep rediscovers the lattice family)

claims.claim: Erdos-Szekeres monotone subsequence lemma: any sequence of (s-1)(t-1)+1 distinct reals contains an increasing subsequence of length s or a decreasing subsequence of length t
claims.label: UNCONDITIONAL-MATHEMATICAL (PROOF.md section 3, complete re-derivation via injective (u,d) labels) + MACHINE-FINITE-CORE (comparator part F: exhaustive over all order types up to length 8, tightness witnesses at length (a-1)(b-1))
claims.content: The full proof is the label-injectivity pigeonhole of PROOF.md section 3; the comparator verifies the finite core exhaustively.

claims.claim: Every k-cup or k-cap (k >= 3) is in convex position
claims.label: UNCONDITIONAL-MATHEMATICAL (PROOF.md section 4, complete induction with the exact cross-product turn inequality)
claims.content: Cups and caps are strictly convex chains; the two endpoints close the polygon.

claims.claim: Dichotomy: any set of binom(a+b-4, a-2)+1 points in GP with pairwise distinct x-coordinates contains an a-cup or a b-cap
claims.label: CITED-CLASSICAL (Erdos-Szekeres 1935; classical proof by induction on a+b with the Pascal recurrence) + MACHINE-CORROBORATED at (a,b) in {(3,3),(3,4),(4,3),(4,4)} (comparator part H; corroboration only — the naive injective-label route FAILS 263/300, receipts107.txt part D)
claims.content: Statement with all hypotheses: GP + pairwise distinct x. This is the engine of the classical upper bound.

claims.claim: Upper bound: every set of binom(2n-4, n-2)+1 points in GP (pairwise distinct x after an arbitrarily small rotation, which preserves GP and convex-position structure) contains a convex n-gon
claims.label: CITED-CLASSICAL (Erdos-Szekeres 1935 dichotomy) + ASSEMBLED (PROOF.md section 5: DICH at (n,n) + CLAIM-CC) + ARITHMETIC-CERTIFIED (comparator part I: the frontier table n=3..40, exact integers)
claims.content: f(n) <= binom(2n-4, n-2)+1; superseded asymptotically by Suk 2017 f(n) <= 2^{(1+o(1))n} and HMPT20 f(n) <= 2^{n+O(sqrt(n log n))} (both cited).

claims.claim: Lower bound: for every n >= 3 there exist 2^{n-2} points in GP with no convex n-gon (Erdos-Szekeres 1961 explicit constructions), hence f(n) >= 2^{n-2}+1
claims.label: CITED-CLASSICAL (Erdos-Szekeres 1961) + MACHINE-WITNESSED at n = 3, 4, 5 (comparator parts A/B/D: the 2-point, 4-point and five 8-point witnesses; the doubling 2 -> 4 -> 8 of the classical construction machine-witnessed)
